profile.headline: Software Engineer at SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory
profile.summary:
• Professional Control Software Engineer with strong experience conducting research in such areas as designing and implementing core algorithms in control, designing and testing dynamic models, formulating ill-defined problems with a data-driven approach, building benchmarks with a proper methodology to test algorithms, delivering high-quality and reliable code for real-time applications in a timely manner, and integrating and testing control systems.
• Strong knowledge and deep understanding of control theory and dynamics, prototyping and implementing controllers on physical systems, and a background in control system design, signal processing, and adaptive control. 
• Proficient in Python, C/C++, and MATLAB/Simulink.

positions.title: INTERN
positions.description:
- Responsible for research and development tasks for power line communication (PLC), such as designing and implementing PLC bus bar, and designing and testing simulation models of systems within the Low Voltage and Systems Integration Team of TESLA in the automobile industry.

Key accomplishments:
- Successfully developed and implemented a program code using MATLAB to calculate impedance characteristics of a complex system from experimental data. This program has resulted in a significant accuracy improvement of 10%.
- Successfully developed and tested simulation models of PLC, 12V lead-acid batteries, and PCBAs.

projects.title: Matpva: Integrate EPICS7 into MATLAB using PVAccess for Python (P4P) module
projects.description: MATLAB is essential for accelerator scientists engaged in data analysis and processing across diverse fields, including particle physics experiments, synchrotron light sources, X-ray Free Electron Lasers (XFELs), and telescopes, due to its extensive range of built-in functions and tools. Scientists also depend on Experimental Physics and Industrial Control Systems (EPICS) 7 to control and monitor complex systems. I have developed Matpva, a Python interface to integrate EPICS 7 with MATLAB. Matpva utilizes the PVAccess for Python (P4P) module and EPICS 7 to offer a robust and reliable interface for MATLAB users that employ EPICS 7. The EPICS 7 PVAccess API allows higher-level scientific applications to get/set/monitor simple and complex structures from an EPICS 7-based control system. Moreover, Matpva simplifies the process by handling the data type conversion from Python to MATLAB, making it easier for researchers to focus on their analyses and innovative ideas instead of technical data conversion. By leveraging Matpva, researchers can work more efficiently and make discoveries in diverse fields, including particle physics and astronomy.
